chapter_mission: Reveal that the wrongness is tied to a failing containment system and force Ben to choose whether to report it or follow it.
chapter_turn: Ben stops being a curious investigator and becomes someone actively hiding a crisis from his own chain of command.

scene_plan.purpose: Bring Ben and Desh into the live perimeter facility and land the warning as an active emergency, not a ruin.
Use the data core to map the Corridor and widen the scale of the problem beyond anything a survey mission can contain.
Make the choice concrete: Ben leaves the alarm unreported, speaks the omission aloud to Desh, and jumps.

relationship_turns.from: co-investigators — sharing the reading of the problem
relationship_turns.to: co-conspirators — Desh names the withholding out loud and stays aboard anyway; the GAG pattern of institutional distance re-activates between them, this time on Ben's initiative
active omission — Ben decides not to report a functioning ancient facility and its distress signal. The distance is now chosen, not incidental

exit_vector: Hyperspace toward uncharted coordinates. The wrongness did not dim on jump; it sharpened. Ben's fingers on the armrest, nav computer painting a route through a chart-sector that does not officially exist. The Lie is operating as urgency. The investigation has become the pursuit.
notes: The facility should feel old, institutional, and still running on duty. Let the report drafts matter as physical evidence that Ben is crossing a line he knows how to name but still refuses to admit.
